PLACES IN THE COMMUNITY LESSON · PLACES IN THE COMMUNITY · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Supermarket — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the whole supermarket trip, from grabbing the cart to the beeping at the till.

What is this?

A supermarket is one big store with all the food in it — fruit, bread, milk, cheese, cereal — lined up in long aisles.

What does it mean?

Gathering is the idea: the whole town&rsquo;s kitchens come shopping in one roof, aisle by aisle.

What does the child need to know?

You need a cart (or a trolley), a list (pictures count!), and your walking feet — the aisles are long and the wheels are tempting.

Why this matters

No family could grow or make everything it eats — the supermarket collects it all so one trip fills a whole week.

What it teaches

List-following, matching picture to shelf, gentle aisle manners (walk, don&rsquo;t wheel), and the checkout sequence — unload, beep, pay, carry.

Words to learn

supermarketstoreshopcarttrolleyaislelisttillcheckoutbag

Say this to your child

“"Cart — check! List — check! Aisle one: apples — found them! Cross it off. The cold aisle — brrr! Milk and cheese. Now the till goes beep, beep, beep — all paid — and I carry the bag. Shopping done!"”

Step by step

  1. Grab a cart — click the wheels, take the driver&rsquo;s seat (for a passenger, that is).
  2. Read the first thing on the list: apples! Now hunt the aisles — apples live with the fruit.
  3. Weigh or count, drop gently in the cart, and cross it off — NEXT!
  4. The cold aisle is an expedition: milk, cheese, yogurt — doors that open into winter.
  5. The till: unload, beep beep beep, pay, and the proud job — carrying the first bag to the car.

Look closer at the picture

On the card, the shopping-cart sign rolls over the supermarket entrance under wide front windows — the sign tells every hungry passerby exactly what happens inside.

Ask your child

"What do we push around the store?" (a cart — or a trolley in the UK) "What is on YOUR list?" "What does the till say when the food goes over it?" (beep, beep, beep)

What your child can say or do

Your child might march the aisles with the list held like a treasure map, interrogate every shelf ("but WHERE do the eggs live?"), or take the bag-carrying job so seriously the bag outlives the shopping.

Out in the real world

American and Canadian families push a shopping cart; British families push a trolley — and the store is a shop on one shore and a store on the other. The picture list is the universal move: every family does it, and it works in all three countries.

Try it together

Home supermarket: cans and boxes lined on a shelf, a basket, a paper list of five foods, and a till that beeps (a spoon on a box works). Shopper shops, cashier beeps, and then the roles swap.

Understanding check

Ask: "What do we bring with us?" (a cart and a list) "What happens at the till?" (beep — pay — carry)

This lesson pairs with the Supermarket flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Places in the Community.
